title: Quantum-Inspired Algorithmic Randomness Generation
abstract: This paper explores the potential of harnessing quantum mechanical principles, specifically superposition and entanglement, to generate truly random numbers. Current classical random number generators rely on entropy sources that, while statistically random, are fundamentally predictable. We propose a novel algorithmic approach termed "Quantum-Inspired Algorithmic Randomness Generation" (Q-IARG) that utilizes controlled quantum decoherence and measurement processes to generate high-entropy random numbers. The core concept involves mapping the probabilistic outcomes of these processes—defined by equations and mathematical models—to a sequence of random numbers. This approach moves beyond merely simulating quantum phenomena and aims for a practically demonstrable improvement in randomness quality. The system is envisioned as a hybrid hardware/software solution, offering a pathway to surpass the limitations of traditional entropy sources. The system's effectiveness will be assessed through the analysis of the statistical properties of the generated sequences, focusing on metrics such as entropy, autocorrelation, and uniformity. This work provides a foundational framework for exploring quantum-inspired randomness generation and its potential applications.

title: Adaptive Neural Symbolic Systems for Complex Reasoning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to complex reasoning by integrating neural networks with symbolic reasoning engines. The core idea is to create an adaptive system where the neural network dynamically adjusts the symbolic representation used for reasoning, based on the problem's complexity. The system utilizes a neural network as a perceptual layer, extracting relevant features and concepts from the input. These extracted concepts are then processed by a symbolic reasoning engine. Crucially, the neural network is trained to refine the symbolic representation, optimizing it for the reasoning task's efficiency and accuracy. This adaptive capability distinguishes this approach from traditional symbolic systems with fixed representations, enabling the system to learn optimal symbolic structures for diverse problems. The resulting Adaptive Neural Symbolic System (ANSS) demonstrates a potential pathway to more robust and flexible reasoning capabilities.

title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence through Symbolic Reasoning Framework
abstract: This paper proposes a framework for achieving explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) by integrating deep learning with symbolic reasoning. The core claim is to translate the predictions of deep learning models into interpretable symbolic rules and then leverage these rules for symbolic reasoning. This framework utilizes knowledge graphs and logic programming to convert the internal representations of deep learning models into symbolic knowledge. The mechanism involves a process of mapping learned features from deep neural networks into a formal knowledge representation, followed by applying logical inference rules to derive new knowledge or explain existing predictions. The novelty lies in the deep fusion of these two approaches, offering a pathway to increased transparency and trustworthiness in AI systems. The proposed framework addresses the limitations of black-box deep learning models by providing a transparent, rule-based explanation of their decisions. This work contributes to the growing field of XAI by offering a concrete methodology for bridging the gap between the statistical power of deep learning and the interpretability of symbolic reasoning.

title: Us vs. Them: A Dataset of Political Othering in Brazilian WhatsApp Discourse
abstract: Political polarization is increasingly expressed through discursive strategies that construct moral and symbolic boundaries between “us” and “them”. Among these strategies, othering is particularly important because it portrays sociopolitical groups as fundamentally different, inferior, or threatening. However, despite extensive research on hate speech and misinformation, othering remains less studied, partly due to the lack of annotated resources that capture this phenomenon. In this paper, we introduce a large-scale labeled dataset for political othering from Brazilian public WhatsApp groups. Starting from a manually annotated gold set, we develop an LLM-assisted annotation pipeline with systematic human validation, resulting in 8.5k labeled messages. Our analysis shows that othering is not limited to explicit insults or traditional hate-speech targets. Instead, it frequently targets ideological, partisan, and institutional opponents through negative affect and the discursive construction of group boundaries. These findings highlight political othering as a distinct dimension of harmful discourse in online environments.

title: Hypergraph Neural Networks for Multi-Relational Data
abstract: Traditional Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have demonstrated remarkable success in modeling relational data. However, their performance often degrades when dealing with datasets exhibiting complex, multi-relational structures, such as those found in knowledge graphs, biological networks, and social networks. This paper introduces a novel approach utilizing Hypergraph Neural Networks (HGNNs) to effectively learn from such data. HGNNs extend the fundamental concepts of GNNs to operate directly on hypergraphs, enabling the representation and propagation of information across multiple connections between nodes. We propose a customized message-passing scheme designed specifically for the higher-order connectivity inherent in hypergraph structures. The core claim of this work is that leveraging hypergraphs offers a significant advantage over traditional GNNs for multi-relational data, leading to improved accuracy and robustness. We demonstrate the efficacy of our approach through theoretical analysis and outline the key components of the HNN architecture. The primary contribution lies in the adaptation of GNN principles to the hypergraph domain, providing a robust framework for capturing intricate relational patterns.

title: Semantic Web Technologies for Automated Theorem Proving
abstract: This paper explores the application of Semantic Web technologies, specifically Resource Description Framework (RDF) and related techniques, to the field of automated theorem proving. The core argument is that the Semantic Web's strengths in knowledge representation – its ability to model complex relationships and facilitate reasoning – can be effectively utilized to enhance and potentially revolutionize automated theorem proving systems. We propose representing mathematical theorems and their corresponding proofs as RDF triples, creating a graph-based representation that allows for automated reasoning and rigorous proof verification through graph traversal and logical inference. This approach offers a novel way to tackle the complexities of automated theorem proving, moving beyond traditional symbolic representations and leveraging the inherent capabilities of the Semantic Web. The work details the design of such a system and discusses potential challenges and future research directions.

title: Quantum Neural Network Architectures Based on Topological Qubits
abstract: This paper explores the design and implementation of quantum neural network (QNN) architectures leveraging the unique properties of topological qubits. Traditional QNNs face significant challenges regarding decoherence and scalability. Utilizing the inherent robustness of topological qubits – specifically their protection against local perturbations – presents a novel approach to constructing more reliable and efficient QNNs. We propose a framework for building QNNs based on topologically protected quantum bits, outlining the core mechanisms for information processing and demonstrating the potential for enhanced training stability. The architecture emphasizes the use of braiding operations to induce entanglement and the subsequent application of quantum algorithms for learning and inference. This work addresses a critical need for robust quantum computing platforms suitable for complex neural network training, moving beyond the limitations of current approaches. The presented architecture offers a pathway towards scalable and fault-tolerant QNNs, representing a significant step in realizing the full potential of quantum computation for artificial intelligence.

title: Quantum Chaos Control
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum chaos control for advanced quantum computation and information processing. We propose a system leveraging the inherent properties of quantum chaos, specifically the extreme sensitivity to initial conditions, to achieve precise control and manipulation of quantum systems. The core mechanism involves inducing and managing quantum chaos within a system of qubits by carefully tuning their parameters. This approach aims to exploit the chaotic dynamics for quantum computation, offering a novel pathway beyond traditional quantum control methods. The theoretical framework presented outlines the design considerations and potential applications of this technique, focusing on harnessing the unique characteristics of chaotic quantum systems. This work establishes a foundation for future research into utilizing quantum chaos as a powerful tool in the development of more robust and versatile quantum computing architectures.

title: Decentralized Learning with Byzantine Fault Tolerance using Compressed Sensing
abstract: Decentralized learning presents significant opportunities for scalable and robust machine learning, but it is inherently vulnerable to malicious actors introducing Byzantine faults – arbitrary updates designed to corrupt the learning process. This paper proposes a novel approach to mitigating these faults by integrating compressed sensing (CS) with Byzantine fault tolerance mechanisms. Our core idea is to leverage CS's ability to reconstruct sparse signals from incomplete measurements to identify anomalous updates originating from compromised nodes. By analyzing the statistical properties of these updates, we can effectively filter out malicious contributions and ensure the convergence of the distributed learning algorithm. We formulate the problem as a robust optimization challenge, where we aim to minimize the impact of Byzantine updates while maximizing the accuracy of the learned model. The theoretical analysis demonstrates the effectiveness of our approach, highlighting its ability to tolerate a significant number of Byzantine nodes. The proposed method offers a practical and efficient solution for building resilient decentralized learning systems, particularly in environments where trust is limited or compromised.

title: Adaptive Quantum Circuit Compilation via Variational Quantum Eigensolver Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum circuit compilation that leverages the feedback capabilities of the Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) to achieve adaptive optimization. Traditional quantum compilation methods are static, assuming a known and consistent noise profile for the target quantum hardware. However, real quantum devices exhibit significant noise variations, leading to suboptimal circuit execution. Our strategy addresses this challenge by dynamically adjusting compilation parameters based on the VQE's error estimations during runtime. The core idea is to implement a real-time optimization loop where the VQE provides error estimates for individual gate operations, and the compiler subsequently modifies the circuit topology and gate choices to minimize overall error. This adaptive compilation scheme allows the quantum circuit to 'learn' the noise characteristics of the hardware, leading to a reduction in gate count and improved fidelity. The presented framework offers a pathway towards more robust and efficient quantum computation, particularly relevant as quantum hardware matures and noise mitigation techniques become more sophisticated. We outline the key components of the system, including the VQE integration, the compilation algorithm, and a discussion of potential challenges and future research directions.

title: Causal Reasoning Graph Neural Networks in Deep Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to deep learning that integrates causal reasoning with Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). The core idea is to construct a neural network model capable of learning causal relationships and performing inference based on those relationships. Traditional deep learning models often struggle to understand and represent causal relationships, leading to limitations in interpretability and robustness. Our approach utilizes causal graphs to analyze input data, identifying potential causal links. Subsequently, a Graph Neural Network is employed to learn the relationships between nodes within the graph, explicitly incorporating these causal relationships into the learning process. This allows the model to perform tasks such as predicting the impact of a causal factor and determining the direct cause of an event. The integration of causal reasoning into GNNs enhances the model's ability to understand and reason about complex systems, ultimately improving both its interpretability and its resilience to spurious correlations. The key contribution lies in providing a framework for building interpretable and robust deep learning models by explicitly modeling causal dependencies.

title: Quantum-Inspired Probabilistic Resonance for Bayesian Networks
abstract: Bayesian network inference remains a computationally intensive task, particularly for large and complex networks. Traditional methods often rely on exhaustive search or approximate techniques that can be slow to converge and may not fully explore the inference space. This paper proposes a novel approach, Quantum-Inspired Probabilistic Resonance (QIPR), which leverages principles from quantum mechanics, specifically superposition and interference, to dramatically enhance Bayesian network inference. The core idea is to introduce a 'resonance' operator that simultaneously evaluates multiple potential belief assignments, akin to quantum interference, guided by the network's structure and prior knowledge. This resonance operator effectively amplifies relevant pathways, accelerating convergence and improving the exploration of the inference space. We detail the mathematical formulation of the QIPR engine, including the probability amplitude calculations and the resonance operator's influence. The methodology offers a potential paradigm shift in Bayesian network inference, offering enhanced efficiency and accuracy in tackling complex probabilistic models. The presented framework provides a robust and adaptable method for Bayesian network inference, addressing limitations of conventional approaches.

title: Quantum State Transformation via Topological Bifurcation and Computation
abstract: Quantum state transformation is a fundamental aspect of quantum computation, and traditional approaches often rely on static mappings. This paper explores the potential of topological bifurcation, a novel technique for dynamically altering quantum states, to unlock more complex computational possibilities. We introduce a framework leveraging topological transformations to reshape quantum states, enabling the creation of novel quantum algorithms and processing paradigms. The core mechanism focuses on inducing non-linear geometric distortions within the quantum state, ultimately leading to enhanced computational capabilities. This work represents a significant step towards adaptive quantum computing, offering a fundamentally different approach to state manipulation and computation.

title: Quantum Simulation of Abstract Algebra
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum simulation to revolutionize the modeling of abstract algebra, addressing limitations of classical approaches. We propose a novel quantum algorithm, Quantum Lattice Construction, designed to iteratively construct and analyze algebraic structures, employing quantum superposition and entanglement to represent and manipulate algebraic concepts. The core claim is that this approach offers a fundamentally new path towards more accurate and efficient abstract algebra representation and analysis. We outline the algorithm's design, discuss its potential benefits, and present preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness in a simplified example. The paper concludes with an assessment of the challenges and future directions for this research.

title: Adaptive Neural Network Architecture
abstract: This paper presents a novel self-adaptive neural network architecture leveraging machine learning to dynamically adjust network structure and parameters. Traditional neural network design relies heavily on human expertise, limiting the network's adaptability. This work introduces a framework that utilizes machine learning to automatically optimize the network's architecture and weights, resulting in improved model performance. The core mechanism centers around a reinforcement learning-based approach to iteratively refine the network's structure based on a predefined set of performance metrics. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through extensive experimentation on a variety of benchmark datasets. The paper provides a comprehensive overview of the proposed architecture, detailing its key components and the underlying learning process.

title: Dynamic Constraint Representation for Evolutionary Algorithms
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic constraint representation system for evolutionary algorithms, enhancing their adaptability and robustness. Traditional evolutionary algorithms often struggle with constraints that shift or become irrelevant during the optimization process. Our approach dynamically updates a 'constraint state' that evolves alongside the population, ensuring that constraints remain relevant and influence the evolutionary process. This leads to more effective and reliable solutions compared to static constraint management. The system's design incorporates a novel mechanism for constraint evolution based on a fitness function, promoting adaptive constraint management. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through several illustrative examples, showcasing improved solution quality and stability.

title: Hierarchical Symbolic Regression with Bayesian Optimization
abstract: Symbolic regression is a powerful technique for discovering mathematical expressions that accurately represent a given dataset. However, its computational cost often becomes prohibitive for complex functions. This work introduces a novel approach, Hierarchical Symbolic Regression with Bayesian Optimization (HRSBO), designed to address this challenge. The core idea is to decompose the symbolic regression problem into a hierarchy of sub-problems, allowing for more focused and efficient searching. Bayesian optimization is then employed to guide the search process at each level of this hierarchy, intelligently selecting the most promising expressions to evaluate. This combination significantly reduces the overall computational burden while maintaining the ability to uncover accurate mathematical models. We demonstrate the effectiveness of HRSBO through a theoretical analysis and a detailed description of the algorithm, highlighting its advantages over traditional symbolic regression methods. The key contribution lies in the synergistic application of hierarchical decomposition and Bayesian optimization, offering a practical and scalable solution for complex symbolic regression problems.

title: Title: Topological Information Extraction via Dynamic Quantum State Modeling
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm for extracting richer topological information from quantum states. Traditional topological analysis often relies on static representations, limiting the ability to fully characterize complex quantum systems. Our approach leverages the inherent dynamism of quantum states to construct a dynamic quantum state model and utilize it for information extraction. The core mechanism involves establishing a model based on quantum state evolution, enabling the identification and representation of intricate topological structures. This innovation promises a more flexible and insightful understanding of quantum phenomena, potentially offering significant advancements in quantum information processing and analysis. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation, highlighting its potential to unlock new insights into quantum systems.

title: Dimension Space Mapping: A Logical and Semantic Analysis
abstract: This paper explores the development of a novel dimensionality mapping method, centered around the principle of translating mathematical concepts and structures into a logical and semantic framework. The core idea is to represent mathematical principles through a set of logical rules, and then leverage this representation through a process of deductive reasoning to derive new mathematical conclusions. This approach aims to enhance the interpretability and operationalizability of mathematical reasoning, moving beyond the limitations of traditional, formula-driven methods. The investigation focuses on establishing a robust mapping system capable of transforming complex mathematical ideas into a structured, understandable logical structure. The paper presents a conceptual framework and preliminary implementation demonstrating the potential for this method to provide a more intuitive and readily applicable approach to mathematical exploration.

title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Intrinsic Motivation for Graph Exploration
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to graph exploration leveraging Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) and intrinsic motivation. The core idea is to train a team of agents to collaboratively navigate and learn within complex graph structures, incentivizing them not solely by external task completion but also by the act of discovering previously unexplored regions of the graph. We introduce a mechanism where agents receive rewards based on both achieved goals and the novelty of their experiences. This intrinsic reward signal drives exploration, significantly improving learning efficiency and the overall ability of the team to uncover hidden structures within the graph. The proposed framework addresses a key challenge in graph-based RL – the difficulty of exploration – by directly incorporating an intrinsic motivation component. Experimental results (simulated) demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach compared to standard MARL methods without intrinsic motivation, showcasing a substantial improvement in graph coverage and learning speed. The key components of this work include a decentralized agent architecture, a tailored intrinsic reward function, and a collaborative learning strategy. Further investigation into the design of appropriate intrinsic reward functions and the scaling of this approach to larger, more complex graphs remains a key area for future research.

title: Artificial Intelligence–Based Assessment of Pathologic Response to Neoadjuvant Chemoimmunotherapy in Non–Small Cell Lung Cancer: An International Multicenter Cohort Study
authors: José Luis Campo-Cañaveral de la Cruz
abstract: BACKGROUND: Pathologic response (PR), expressed as the percentage of residual viable tumor (%RVT), has emerged as a surrogate endpoint after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, PR assessment remains subject to interobserver variability and is insufficiently standardized across institutions and clinical trials. We hypothesized that artificial intelligence (AI)-based %RVT scoring would be concordant with expert manual assessment and consistent across real-world, multi-scanner cohorts. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Four retrospective NSCLC cohorts treated with neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy and surgery were analyzed. The internal cohort included 38 patients; three external cohorts from China, Germany, and Spain contributed 97 additional patients. Weighted consensus manual %RVT served as the reference standard for benchmarking an AI algorithm. Discordant cases were interrogated for algorithmic bias. RESULTS: Overall, 135 patients and 1,344 primary-tumor H&E slides were evaluable. Concordance between AI-based and manual assessment was at least moderate across all cohorts. For major pathologic response (MPR) classification, the AI algorithm achieved a pooled accuracy of 91% (95% CI, 85-95), sensitivity of 90% (82-95), specificity of 93% (81-99), and an area under the curve ≥0.95 in all cohorts. Discordant classifications occurred in 8.9% of cases and were mainly attributable to stromal underrepresentation and misclassification of non-neoplastic elements. CONCLUSIONS: AI-based %RVT scoring was concordant with expert pathologist consensus and consistent across real-world, multicenter, multi-scanner cohorts, with most algorithmic errors mirroring those encountered in human practice. By providing explainable %RVT grounded in international recommendations, our framework may facilitate harmonization of PR assessment for perioperative therapies.

title: EgoNeMo: Transferable Map of Pedestrian Dynamics via Egocentric LiDAR Scan
abstract: This paper proposes a transferable Map of Dynamics (MoD) framework that generalizes to unknown environments using only egocentric 3D LiDAR point clouds to overcome the long-standing limitation of traditional MoD methods. While MoDs are essential for encoding human motion characteristics to enable accurate pedestrian trajectory prediction or safe robot navigation, traditional approaches suffer from site-specificity, requiring exhaustive trajectory accumulation at every new location. Extending recent advances in neural implicit modeling, our framework trains a continuous, LiDAR-based MoD estimator across diverse environments. To mitigate the inherent sparsity and temporal bias of real-world trajectory data, we introduce a position-balanced sampling strategy and a multi-task learning architecture that jointly predicts motion distributions and a spatial frequency score map. The latter is further augmented by visibility-aware losses to compensate for incomplete observation data. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that our method effectively reconstructs underlying motion maps even in unknown locations from a single instantaneous LiDAR scan, despite highly sparse training data. Finally, we show that our improvements enhance the reliability of downstream trajectory prediction.

title: ProtoRAG: Prototype-Based Retrieval Augmentation for Few-Shot Fine-Grained Remote Sensing Object Detection
abstract: Few-shot fine-grained object detection (FGOD) in remote sensing imagery is challenging because limited annotations must support both object localization and discrimination among visually similar subcategories. Although multimodal large language models (MLLMs) provide strong coarse object localization, they lack explicit visual evidence for reliable fine-grained recognition. To address this limitation, we propose ProtoRAG, a prototype-based retrieval-augmented framework that decouples coarse localization from fine-grained recognition by equipping MLLMs with an external object-level visual memory. To construct a reliable visual memory from limited support samples, we introduce Discriminative Prototype Space Learning (DPSL), which encourages discriminative and prototype-stable representations through supervised contrastive learning and prototype-consistency regularization. We further develop an uncertainty-guided candidate-constrained reasoning strategy that augments MLLMs with retrieved candidate-specific visual references and invokes multimodal reasoning only for ambiguous instances. Extensive experiments show that ProtoRAG consistently surpasses representative baselines in nine few-shot settings, outperforming the strongest baselines by 14.80, 2.27, and 4.04 mAP$_{50}$ on MAR20, HRSC2016, and FAIR1M-2.0, respectively.

title: AGENTRUN: Failure-Driven QLoRA Specialization for Multi-Tool Agent Behavior in a 7B Language Model
abstract: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning is widely assumed to improve small open-weight models on the specific behaviors it targets. We present a controlled case study that complicates this assumption for multi-tool agent execution. Using Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and a fixed 23-task, machine-checkable benchmark, we show that an initial 35-trajectory QLoRA adapter (v1) regresses from the base model's 22/23 (95.7%) to 18/23 (78.3%)—despite the training data being disjoint from the benchmark at the prompt level. Trace-level inspection of every failure attributes the regression to two distinct causes: a serving-layer tool-call parsing defect, and insufficient coverage of chained and error-handling tool-use patterns in the training data. Correcting the parser and adding 11 trajectories targeting the observed failure categories yields v2, which passes all 23 tasks. We treat this recovery cautiously: because the augmentation categories were selected by inspecting which benchmark categories failed, the result is better characterized as closing an identified, benchmark-specific gap than as evidence of improved general tool-use ability, and we report a category-level train/eval information leakage threat that this design introduces. Using the recorded failure traces, we further separate, to the extent the evidence allows, which recovered failures are attributable to the parser fix versus the data augmentation. We release the evaluation harness, training data, serving code, and full result artifacts to support replication and critique.

title: Distributed Differential Privacy via Secure Multiparty Computation for Federated Learning
abstract: Federated learning (FL) offers a promising approach to training machine learning models on decentralized data sources without directly exchanging data. However, this approach inherently exposes sensitive user data, raising significant privacy concerns. This paper proposes a novel framework for distributed differential privacy (DDP) within a secure multiparty computation (SMC) environment for FL. The core idea is to utilize SMC to guarantee differential privacy while minimizing communication overhead and computational complexity. Our protocol constructs a distributed computation where each client contributes to a shared global model update, shielded by the privacy guarantees of differential privacy. The proposed system aims to achieve a strong privacy-utility trade-off, addressing a critical gap in existing FL solutions. We formally define the system, outline the protocol, and analyze its privacy and computational characteristics. The key contributions lie in the synergistic combination of SMC and differential privacy within a federated setting, providing a robust solution for privacy-preserving machine learning.

title: Hierarchical Graph Embedding for Large-Scale Networks
abstract: Graph embedding techniques have gained significant traction in recent years for representing complex networks in a low-dimensional vector space. However, a major bottleneck in applying these methods to large-scale networks is the computational cost associated with learning embeddings for all nodes simultaneously. This paper proposes a novel hierarchical graph embedding approach designed to overcome this scalability challenge. The core idea is to decompose the large graph into smaller, manageable subgraphs, learn embeddings for each subcomponent independently, and subsequently combine these sub-embeddings to generate a comprehensive representation of the entire graph. This hierarchical structure dramatically reduces the computational burden while preserving valuable network information. We detail the algorithm, discuss its theoretical underpinnings, and outline potential extensions and future research directions. Our approach offers a practical solution for embedding large networks efficiently and effectively.

title: Self-Supervised Learning with Contrastive Predictive Coding and Graph Structures
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to self-supervised learning that leverages the power of contrastive predictive coding (CPC) in conjunction with graph structures. The core idea is to enhance CPC's ability to learn meaningful representations by explicitly modeling dependencies within the data using graph representations. We extend the CPC framework to operate on nodes within a graph, where edges are learned through a predictive modeling process. This allows the model to capture and utilize contextual information, leading to improved representation learning. The experimental design focuses solely on demonstrating the theoretical potential and efficacy of this combined approach, without requiring empirical validation through data experiments. The key contribution lies in the theoretical framework and the proposed mechanism for integrating graph structures into CPC. This represents a significant step toward more robust and effective self-supervised learning, particularly in scenarios where data exhibits complex interdependencies. The primary formulation of the method is presented, along with a detailed explanation of the mathematical underpinnings.

title: From Probabilistic Cloud to Pycloud — A Control-Layer Language for Quantum Computing and Hardware Validation
abstract: Probabilistic cloud state machine (PCSM) theory [1] formalises the classical control layer of quantum computation as a geometric model on the space of stable probability distributions. The six-layer technology stack is: physical calibration layer, symbol-table layer, structure layer, semantic-resolution layer, compiler layer, and pycloud API layer. Hardware results: (1) the anchoring fidelity of single-qubit and two-qubit symbols in a single hardware calibration session is A=0.889–0.998A=0.889–0.998 (√JS convention; for the two-qubit conversions see the data note of §5.3, where the unusable symbol AA is as low as 0.22 — the two-qubit symbol h_i, whose old-convention value 0.5836 is stored in pycloud/data/wukong_2qubit_symbols.json and whose √JS-convention value is 0.2249); the upper bound of deterministic symbols is about A≈0.915A≈0.915, determined by the readout error and not improvable by more shots (§4.2); (2) parametrised rotation gates show significant anomalies at specific angles (RY(π/4) deviation 0.136 ≈ 8.6σ, RZ(π/2) deviation 0.167 ≈ 7.4σ), while RY(0), RY(π/2) and RY(π) are normal; the discrete gates (H, X, CNOT, S) are normal in this dataset (§4.4). This paper reports the anomaly truthfully and states that the present data are insufficient to determine the root cause; (3) the three-qubit GHZ state yields M=3.9541M=3.9541 and M=3.9720M=3.9720 in two measurements, both far beyond the classical bound 2, confirming the physical realisability of multipartite entanglement (§4.5). The two measurements are technical replicates with the same circuit, the same device and the same calibration window, and do not constitute independent experiments; (4) a recalibration record of 40 intermittent sampling points (2026-09-05 08:34–15:08, spanning about 6.6 hours, 500 shots per point) shows that the standard deviation of P(0)P(0) of the ∣+⟩∣+⟩ symbol prepared by the H gate is 2.71 times the pure shot-noise expectation, and the mean deviates from 0.5 by 5.6 standard errors — a real deviation beyond statistical fluctuation; hence "calibrate once, use indefinitely" is unreliable (§4.3). Note: the sampling is intermittent, and no drift rate or time scale is claimed on this basis; (5) the theory paper gives two ceilings for the control layer: the first is the hardware layer (the readout error determines A≤0.915A≤0.915, §4.2); the second is the coherence blind spot (theorem-level, hardware-independent): ∣+⟩∣+⟩ and ∣−⟩∣−⟩ have classical anchoring A=1A=1 and are completely indistinguishable in the computational basis, while their quantum JS distance is the maximum ln⁡2ln2 — regardless of shots and readout quality, the control layer's ability to distinguish the family of same-diagonal pairs is identically zero (§5.6). This paper further gives a third ceiling (predictive-gain ceiling, theorem-level, hardware-independent): for the ensemble {12,∣+⟩;12,∣−⟩}{21,∣+⟩;21,∣−⟩}, the Holevo quantity is χ=ln⁡2χ=ln2 while the control layer's relationality is I=0I=0 (I≤χI≤χ, the fourth row of the fourfold projection) — the control layer's predictive gain on the family of same-diagonal pairs is identically zero (§5.6). "Symbols must be bound to a measurement basis" is thereby promoted from an engineering requirement to a necessity of the projection structure; (6) directionality monitoring primitive: the third cumulant TT and the asymmetry difference (the difference of the two KL divergences, ≈−16T dθ3≈−61Tdθ3) can serve as a directionality probe into the blind spot of second-order statistics (AA), for testing the relation between directionality defects and the parametrised-gate anomalies (§5.7, not yet on hardware · proposal); (7) mathematical grounding (based on the mathematics paper [10]; no hardware data are changed): the three edge-definition conditions of §2.4 are the engineering instances of Theorems 2 and 3 of the mathematics paper; the symbol drift of §5.1 is the theoretically expected failure of the regularity condition R3 (the recalibration loop is the quasi-stationary compensation); the directionality monitoring of §5.7 gains logical-side support from Theorems 7 and 4; the structure layer of §2.6 is an instance of the structure–symbol sample space (mathematics paper Definitions 2.1/2.2); the priority 0 of §8.2 acquires theoretical necessity. Convention note: the theoretical presentation of this paper is aligned with the four-dimensional convention of Constraints of Logical Space [11] — the four dimensions are directionality ΔSΔS, determinacy HH, consistency (anchoring strength) AA, and relationality II, whose quantum completion is the fourfold projection (H≥SvNH≥SvN, ΔS≤SqΔS≤Sq, JS≤JQJS≤JQ, I≤χI≤χ); the name of the third dimension is consistency, AA being the anchoring strength, and "anchoring fidelity" is the engineering metric name retained in this paper. Keywords: probabilistic cloud state machine; quantum programming language; pycloud; anchoring fidelity; hardware validation; GHZ; Mermin inequality; Origin Wukong; coherence blind spot; predictive-gain ceiling; (运行时)pycloud API 提供运行时指令 WAIT/RESET/TRACE/SAVE_CONTEXT,配合上下文数据结构 ContextData(符号表 + 边表 + 任务 ID + 操作历史 + 资源分配快照)实现运行时状态的可保存、可加载、可审计(§7.5); (调度器)静态调度器(优先级降序 → 比特数过滤 → 最低噪声贪心分配)与动态调度器(噪声漂移模拟 + 执行时间管理 + 异常处理)原型完成:模拟中 reg_A 噪声升至 0.09 时,受影响的 p_Bell 任务自动迁移至 reg_E,reg_A 进入重标定态并在两个时间步后恢复(§7.3–7.4)——这是"符号表必须动态标定"在运行时层的工程实现; (三比特符号)在本源悟空典型噪声模型(去极化 0.001、读出误差 0.01)下构建三比特仿真符号表:8 个候选符号全部通过一致性筛选(√JS 约定,A≈0.975–0.990),去冗余后保留 7 个(含 GHZ 态,A=0.97506)【离线仿真】(§7.2); (测试)测试套件 38 项全部通过,覆盖编译器、符号表、结构图、调度器、数值精度、边界情形与集成路径(§7.6)。 真机结果: (1)单比特与两比特符号在单次真机标定中的锚定保真度为 A=0.889–0.998A=0.889–0.998(JSJS 约定;两比特符号的换算见 §5.3 数据注记,其中不可用符号 AA 低至 0.22——即两比特符号 h_i,其旧约定值 0.5836 存储于 pycloud/data/wukong_2qubit_symbols.json,√JS 约定值为 0.2249);确定性符号的上限约 A≈0.915A≈0.915,该上限由读出误差决定,提高 shots 不能改善(§4.2); (2)参数化旋转门在特定角度出现显著异常(RY(π/4) 偏差 0.136 ≈ 8.6σ、RZ(π/2) 偏差 0.167 ≈ 7.4σ),而 RY(0)、RY(π/2)、RY(π) 正常;离散门(H、X、CNOT、S)本次数据正常(§4.4)。本文如实报告该异常,并说明现有数据不足以判定根因; (3)三比特 GHZ 态两次测得 M=3.9541M=3.9541 与 M=3.9720M=3.9720,均远超经典极限 2,确认多体纠缠的物理可实现性(§4.5)。两次测量为同一线路、同一校准窗口内的技术重复,不构成独立实验; title: A Proof System Based on Scalable Approximate Reasoning
abstract: This paper presents a novel proof system designed to tackle large-scale theorem proving challenges. The system leverages approximate reasoning techniques to reduce the complexity of proofs and employs distributed computing to enable parallelization and accelerated proof generation. The core innovation lies in the combination of these approaches, offering a scalable solution where traditional methods struggle. We explore the underlying mathematical framework, focusing on the approximation algorithms and distributed computation strategies that enable efficient proof generation. The system is built around a core mechanism of iteratively refining approximate solutions, ultimately converging towards a valid proof. This work contributes to the broader field of automated theorem proving by providing a practical methodology for handling computationally intensive problems. ---

title: Based on Quantum Entanglement Distributed Semantic Understanding Engine
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to semantic understanding leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. Traditional semantic understanding systems rely on probabilistic models and rule-based systems, often struggling with the inherent ambiguity and complexity of natural language. We introduce a distributed semantic understanding engine based on quantum entanglement, aiming to achieve a deeper and more nuanced understanding of complex semantic information. The core claim is that utilizing the non-local correlations inherent in quantum entanglement can surpass the limitations of conventional information representation and processing. The system architecture consists of a network of quantum processors, each responsible for processing a portion of the semantic data. A carefully designed quantum entanglement protocol establishes quantum channels between processors, facilitating the encoding of information correlations and dependencies at a quantum level. Distributed semantic reasoning is performed using entangled states, and quantum error correction techniques are employed to enhance computational reliability. We explore the theoretical possibilities and potential advantages of this approach, emphasizing its departure from classical methods and its potential to unlock a fundamentally different paradigm for semantic understanding. This research addresses the need for more robust and accurate semantic analysis in scenarios involving high-dimensional data and complex relationships. ---

title: Quantum Walk-Based Graph Search Algorithms
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum walk algorithms for graph search problems. Classical graph search algorithms, such as Dijkstra's algorithm, frequently encounter limitations when dealing with large graphs, often exhibiting performance bottlenecks due to exhaustive exploration of the graph's nodes. We propose a novel approach utilizing quantum walks to address these challenges. Quantum walks exploit quantum superposition and interference to facilitate a more efficient exploration of the graph space compared to their classical counterparts. The theoretical framework presented investigates the potential for exponential speedups in graph search operations. We formally define the quantum walk model and its implementation for graph traversal, outlining the key steps involved in constructing a quantum algorithm. This work focuses on the theoretical aspects of the algorithm, providing a foundation for future experimental investigations and optimization.

title: Adaptive Topology Calculation Cryptography
abstract: This paper introduces Adaptive Topology Calculation Cryptography (ATCC), a novel computational framework for enhancing cryptographic security through the strategic application of adaptive topology. We propose a new approach that dynamically adjusts the underlying topology of cryptographic primitives, resulting in enhanced resistance to attacks based on known structure analysis. The system's core mechanism involves a layered approach to topology manipulation, incorporating both structural analysis and adaptive reconstruction to mitigate vulnerabilities. This paper explores the potential of ATCC to significantly improve data security and privacy through novel cryptographic algorithms and enhanced security protocols. We detail the design, implementation, and evaluation of the framework, highlighting its strengths and limitations.

title: 基于图的逻辑推理算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm for logical reasoning based on graph theory and node relationships. Traditional approaches often rely on explicit rules and deductive reasoning, while our method leverages the inherent topology of graphs and the interconnected nature of nodes to efficiently represent and solve complex logical inference problems. The core mechanism involves transforming logical reasoning questions into computational problems, employing graph traversal and node manipulation to automate the reasoning process. This algorithm offers a significant advancement in logical reasoning by effectively capturing the inherent complexity of logical inference. The proposed approach demonstrates improved performance and scalability for a range of challenging logical problems.

title: EXITO Y FRACASOS DE LA IA EN LAS EMPRESAS
abstract: En los últimos años, prácticamente no ha existido una junta directiva, un reporte anual o una feria de negocios en la que no se hable de inteligencia artificial (IA). Las empresas, grandes y pequeñas, se han lanzado a integrar chatbots, asistentes automáticos, sistemas de análisis de datos y herramientas generativas en sus procesos, con la promesa de volverse más eficientes, más rentables y más competitivas. Sin embargo, detrás de ese entusiasmo generalizado hay una realidad mucho menos comentada ya que la mayoría de estos proyectos no está dando los resultados que se esperaban. Este contraste entre la enorme inversión que las empresas están haciendo en IA y los resultados reales que obtienen es lo que se conoce, en algunos estudios recientes, como la “brecha de la IA generativa”. Por un lado, hay compañías que han logrado ahorros importantes, procesos más rápidos y hasta nuevas fuentes de ingresos gracias a la IA. Por otro lado, la mayoría de las organizaciones que han probado estas herramientas reportan que, después de meses de trabajo y de gasto de dinero, no ven ningún cambio significativo en sus resultados financieros. Entender qué separa a unas empresas de otras es el propósito central de este ensayo. El tema tiene un fondo social importante que va más allá de la tecnología en sí misma. Cuando una empresa invierte en IA sin obtener resultados, no solo pierde dinero, sino que también puede despedir personal de forma innecesaria, frustrar a sus equipos de trabajo, y perder terreno frente a competidores que sí lograron integrar la tecnología de manera inteligente. Además, las decisiones que toman las empresas sobre IA afectan directamente el tipo de empleos que existirán en el futuro, la manera en que se organiza el trabajo, y hasta la confianza que la sociedad tiene en estas nuevas tecnologías. El objetivo de este ensayo es revisar, con base en estudios recientes de instituciones como el MIT, RAND Corporation, McKinsey y Harvard Business Review, qué factores explican el éxito o el fracaso de las empresas que han integrado la inteligencia artificial en sus procesos. Para lograrlo, el trabajo sigue la estructura habitual de una investigación social: planteamiento del problema, pregunta de investigación, hipótesis, teoría, metodología, resultados y conclusión.

title: Hyperdimensional Symbolic Computation for Semantic Reasoning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel computational framework, Hyperdimensional Symbolic Computation (HSC), designed to address the limitations of traditional symbolic AI in handling complex semantic reasoning. HSC leverages the representational capacity of hypervectors – high-dimensional vectors – combined with a symbolic computation method utilizing vector operations. The core idea is to encode semantic concepts as hypervectors and perform reasoning by manipulating these vectors through operations such as addition, dot product, and rotation, all optimized for semantic similarity assessment and inference. Unlike existing approaches that treat hypervectors primarily as feature representations or solely as probabilistic models, HSC explicitly integrates a symbolic computation layer, enabling the derivation of logical conclusions and the construction of complex semantic networks. We propose a novel algorithm, the Rotational Symbolic Inference Engine (RSIE), for HSC, demonstrating its potential for robust and nuanced semantic reasoning. The presented approach offers a promising direction for building more intelligent systems capable of understanding and reasoning about complex concepts.

title: 基于自适应图论的自适应机器学习算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel machine learning algorithm based on adaptive graph theory, termed "Dynamic Graph Optimization" (DGO). DGO leverages the principles of graph theory to dynamically adjust the structure of the model's representation, thereby enhancing the model's generalization capabilities. The core mechanism centers around a system of graph representations, where the graph's nodes represent data points and edges represent relationships between them. The algorithm iteratively refines these representations through a series of optimization steps, resulting in a model that is more robust and adaptable to new data. This paper provides a detailed explanation of the DGO algorithm, including the mathematical framework and implementation details. The key contribution lies in the novel approach to graph representation and optimization, offering a significant advancement over traditional methods.

title: Neural Turing Machines with Episodic Memory and Contextual Attention
abstract: Neural Turing Machines (NTMs) represent a significant step towards creating neural networks capable of learning algorithmic reasoning. However, their performance is often hindered by the difficulty in managing long-term dependencies and maintaining context over extended sequences. This work introduces a novel architecture that combines the strengths of NTMs with two key components: an episodic memory module and a contextual attention mechanism. The episodic memory provides a structured storage for past experiences, represented as tuples of (s_i, a_i, o_i), where s_i is the input sequence, a_i is the action taken, and o_i is the output. The contextual attention mechanism dynamically weights the relevance of these memories during processing, allowing the NTM to selectively retrieve and utilize pertinent information. This integration significantly enhances the NTM's ability to learn complex tasks requiring long-range dependencies. The system is described by the following equations: Let *Ct* be the current context vector at time step *t*. *Ct* = *fC*( *Ct-1*, *st*, *at*, *μt*) where *fC* is the context update function. The attention weights *μt* are calculated as: *μt* = softmax( *Wa* * *Ct*) where *Wa* is a trainable weight matrix. The output *ot* is determined by: *ot* = *go*( *Ct*, *μt*) where *go* is the output function. The episodic memory is updated using: *Mt* = *Mt-1* ∪ {( *st*, *at*, *ot*)} where *Mt* is the memory at time step *t*. The retrieval of memory is performed as: *rt* = argmaxi | *Wm* * (*Ct*, *si*) | where *Wm* is a trainable weight matrix and *rt* is the index of the most relevant memory. This architecture provides a robust framework for tackling sequential tasks with complex dependencies.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Constraint Satisfaction Problems via Graph Traversal
abstract: Constraint Satisfaction Problems (CSPs) are a fundamental class of computational problems prevalent in various fields, including artificial intelligence, optimization, and cryptography. Traditional CSP solvers often struggle with the exponential complexity associated with large, complex graphs. This research investigates the potential of quantum algorithms, specifically those utilizing quantum walks, to significantly accelerate the solution process for CSPs. We propose a framework that maps CSP instances onto graphs and employs quantum walk algorithms to efficiently traverse the solution space. title: RenewableXAI: Model-Exact Explanation Stability for Renewable Energy Forecasting – Software and Evaluation Artifact
abstract: RenewableXAI is a fully implemented system for interactive inspection of renewable-energy forecasting models. The system combines semantically grouped TreeSHAP explanations, model-exact one-feature explanation-stability intervals, adjacent boundary-transition analysis, interactive scenario editing, and an evidence-constrained local language interface. This research artifact contains the source code, photovoltaic and wind-power domain adapters, frozen holdout question sets, expected question plans, per-route evaluation outputs, deterministic validation decisions, aggregate evaluation reports, independent oracle tests for stability intervals, and integrity manifests. title: A sensitivity-aware privacy budget selection framework for EEG data under local differential privacy
abstract: Protecting sensitive biomedical data is a critical security challenge in decentralized healthcare environments without a trusted authority. Electroencephalography (EEG) signals constitute highly sensitive biometric data used for neurological disorder diagnosis, making privacy-preserving analysis essential. Local differential privacy (LDP) addresses this challenge by perturbing data at the source; however, selecting an appropriate privacy budget $$\varepsilon$$ remains nontrivial, as it directly governs the privacy–utility trade-off. This work proposes a sensitivity-aware privacy budget selection framework for EEG-based analysis under LDP, leveraging multi-criteria decision making to jointly consider privacy level, data accuracy, computational cost, and data sensitivity. Unlike existing approaches that rely on a single global privacy budget, the proposed framework performs participant-specific privacy budget selection, accounting for differences in data sensitivity across participating data sources. Privacy budgets are adaptively selected using TOPSIS and Fuzzy TOPSIS, enabling sensitivity-aware calibration without modifying the underlying LDP mechanism. Experiments conducted on the University of Bonn EEG dataset employ time-domain, frequency-domain, nonlinear, and wavelet features, with eight machine learning classifiers evaluated on privacy-preserving data against a noise-free baseline. The results show that Fuzzy TOPSIS consistently selects smaller privacy budgets, achieving stronger privacy guarantees while maintaining a favorable balance between privacy protection and classification performance. Performance remains stable across classifiers, and the additional computational overhead is modest. Overall, the findings demonstrate that sensitivity-aware privacy budget selection enables effective privacy–utility trade-offs for EEG analysis, offering a scalable and ethically grounded solution for privacy-preserving biomedical signal processing in decentralized healthcare systems.

title: An Improved iTransformer for Day-Ahead Photovoltaic Power Forecasting Based on Frequency Domain and Periodic Modeling
abstract: Abstract Photovoltaic (PV) power day-ahead forecasting is crucial for grid dispatch and energy management, yet its accuracy is severely challenged by the nonstationarity and multiscale periodicity of the power series. To address the limitations of existing transformer models in explicit periodic modeling and handling nonstationary disturbances, this paper proposes an enhanced iTransformer model that integrates frequency-domain decoupling and periodic perception mechanisms. The framework features two key contributions. First, a multiscale contextual temporal query attention mechanism is introduced to enhance the explicit characterization of periodic structures through learnable cycle-aware queries and contextual convolution. Second, an attention-enhanced frequency-informed normalization module is incorporated into the framework to decouple the series into periodic and residual components via Fourier transform. By employing cross-attention for feature enhancement and fusion, this module improves robustness against nonstationary disturbances, such as abrupt weather changes. Extensive day-ahead forecasting experiments on multiple real-world PV plant datasets demonstrate that the proposed model achieves competitive performance against various baseline models across mean squared error, mean absolute error, and weighted absolute percentage error metrics. These results validate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed approach in modeling complex and nonstationary PV power generation patterns.

title: Predicting Wind Turbine Power Using Machine Learning and Weather Forecasts
abstract: Offshore wind turbines are widely used to generate renewable energy, but their maintenance can result in decreased efficiency due to forced shutdowns. Accurate wind turbine power predictions can identify periods of low power that would be ideal for scheduling maintenance. However, the effects of data volume, feature selection, and data preprocessing on the performance of such power prediction models have not been thoroughly studied. Besides, current models have limited transferability between different wind turbines. Therefore, this study developed a baseline Linear Regression for performance comparison with a more complex Artificial Neural Network model to predict the power output of a wind turbine, using weather conditions only to enhance applicability. A range of data preprocessing techniques were studied, and models were trained on one month and one year of data to determine the effects of data preprocessing and volume on model performance. Feature selection was explored using a Random Forest Regressor. The best results from the different models showed that the Artificial Neural Network models provided the highest accuracy, with an R2 score of 0.98 and a low Mean Absolute Error of 194, when compared with the baseline model (R2 score of 0.94 and Mean Absolute Error of 441). The model performance is comparable to the range of results in past studies, with the advantage that the proposed method leverages a separate weather dataset from a nearby weather station, enabling future applications for similar wind turbines in different locations. The Artificial Neural Network model was then used to identify 4-h periods of low power predictions over 2 months (simulating application for future periods), providing power output savings of approximately 2000 kW for each maintenance event.

title: Mooré Greeting Speech Dataset for English Language Learning
abstract: This dataset contains Mooré speech recordings collected and used for the development and preliminary evaluation of a voice-centered mobile application for English language learning in Burkina Faso. The recordings support a closed-vocabulary speech-recognition component based on MFCC features and BiLSTM models. The dataset is provided for research and educational purposes.

title: EOA Vector Generator Tool
abstract: Purpose This tool is a bulk vector generator for the Engineering of Alphabets (EOA) Program. It converts large word lists into EOA-43 vectors with a single click, supporting both real-world vocabulary datasets and custom word lists. Key Features: Feature Description Bulk word list processing Generate EOA-43 vectors for 50k, 100k, 166k, 235k, or 466k word lists instantly. Custom word lists Upload your own .txt file or paste words manually. Client-side only Original sequences NEVER leave your browser. Only word vectors are exported. CSV export Export all generated vectors as a single CSV file. Fixed letter indexing Index is fixed: a=1, b=2, ..., z=26. What the Tool Does Accepts JSON input for 26 letter sequences (a–z). Generates EOA-43 vectors for any list of words. Supports real-world word lists: wordfreq 50k (most common English) wordfreq 100k (most common English) SCOWL 166k (comprehensive dictionary) NLTK Words (235,000 words) dwl 466k (largest word list) SST-2 Vocabulary (~10,000 movie review words) Allows custom word lists via .txt upload or manual entry. Exports all generated vectors as CSV. Figure 1. EOA Vector Generator Input A JSON file containing 43‑term numerical sequences for each letter (a–z). A word list (.txt file or manual paste). Method Each letter maps to a fixed 43‑term sequence. Word vector is built by summing per-letter sequences, weighted by position and alphabetical index. Output EOA-43 vectors for every word in the list. Export as CSV (contains ONLY word vectors — NO letter sequences). Implementation Runs entirely client-side as one self-contained HTML file — no install, no server, no external dependencies beyond a modern browser. Related Work This tool supports the empirical results reported in: EOA Program, Part 0: The Engineering of Alphabets as an Open Frontier EOA Program, Part I: EOA-43: A Rank-Collapsed Deterministic Symbolic Representation Access This tool is part of the Research Disclosure Program described in the EOA papers. Access is granted for research purposes upon request. Contact: bdarghamneurolabs@gmail.com

title: Quantum-Inspired Simulation of Chaotic Systems with Reservoir Computing
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to simulating chaotic systems by integrating reservoir computing with quantum-inspired concepts. Reservoir computing, traditionally utilized for its effectiveness in capturing temporal dynamics, is enhanced by introducing the notion of superposition within the reservoir nodes. This allows for a more accurate and efficient simulation of chaotic attractors and their complex dynamics. The core of the method lies in designing a reservoir network where nodes are governed by rules mimicking quantum superposition, enabling them to represent and evolve within the intricate phase space of chaotic systems. We demonstrate the potential of this combined technique for simulating a variety of chaotic systems, offering an alternative pathway to understanding and modeling complex, nonlinear behavior. The results indicate a significant improvement in accuracy and computational efficiency compared to traditional reservoir computing approaches, particularly when dealing with highly sensitive chaotic systems. Further research will focus on optimizing the reservoir architecture and exploring the application of this method to different chaotic systems and potentially extending it to quantum simulation itself.

title: Self-Supervised Learning of Relational Embeddings from Unlabeled Graph Data
abstract: Graph embeddings have emerged as a powerful technique for representing graph-structured data in a continuous vector space. Traditionally, learning these embeddings has relied heavily on supervised methods, necessitating the availability of labeled data that explicitly defines node relationships. This work presents a novel self-supervised learning approach designed to directly learn graph embeddings from unlabeled graph data. The core idea is to leverage the inherent structural information within the graph to define pretext tasks that can be solved without requiring any external labels. These pretext tasks include node clustering, link prediction, and graph completion, which are used to train an embedding model. The resulting embeddings capture valuable relational information, offering a significant advantage over methods that depend on labeled data. This approach provides a scalable and flexible solution for learning graph embeddings in scenarios where labeled data is scarce or unavailable. The effectiveness of this method is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and a discussion of potential applications.

title: Based on Differential Privacy Federated Learning Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel federated learning optimization algorithm that integrates differential privacy mechanisms to safeguard user data privacy while simultaneously enhancing learning efficiency. Federated learning, while promising for distributed model training, presents significant privacy challenges. Our proposed algorithm addresses this by introducing a privacy-preserving layer directly within the gradient update process, mitigating the risk of sensitive data leakage. We demonstrate through theoretical analysis and a detailed algorithm description that our approach achieves a robust balance between privacy protection and model accuracy, offering a viable solution for privacy-sensitive federated learning applications. The core claim of this work is to propose an optimization algorithm based on differential privacy for federated learning, protecting user data privacy while improving learning efficiency. The core mechanism is introducing a privacy-protecting mechanism in the gradient update process of federated learning to prevent user data leakage.

title: Generative Adversarial Networks for Discovering Novel Graph Kernels
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to the automated discovery of novel graph kernels. Traditional graph kernel design relies heavily on human expertise and intuition, often leading to kernels that are tailored to specific datasets and may not generalize well. We propose a framework where a GAN is trained to generate graph kernels, with a discriminator evaluating their effectiveness in predicting target variables. The generator's objective is to produce kernels that maximize predictive accuracy, essentially learning to capture underlying data relationships without explicit human guidance. This approach offers the potential to identify kernels surpassing those designed manually, significantly accelerating the kernel discovery process and potentially unlocking previously unseen patterns within graph-structured data. The core of this work lies in the adversarial training process, establishing a dynamic equilibrium between kernel generation and performance evaluation, leading to optimized kernels for diverse applications. The results demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of leveraging GANs for automated graph kernel discovery.

title: Quantum Machine Learning: Geometric Mapping for Optimal Parameter Optimization
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) offers a paradigm shift in computation, potentially unlocking unprecedented capabilities in areas like drug discovery, materials science, and optimization. This paper investigates the application of geometric mapping to QML, specifically focusing on optimizing quantum model parameters through the application of geometric transformations. We propose a novel framework that utilizes geometric properties to guide the parameter search process, leading to improved model accuracy and efficiency. This research explores the benefits of this approach compared to traditional machine learning techniques, particularly in the context of quantum systems. The core mechanism involves mapping a quantum system's state space to a geometric space, leveraging geometric properties to enhance the optimization process. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential impact of this geometric mapping technique on the future of QML.

title: Fractal Geometry-Based Error Correction Codes
abstract: This paper explores the application of fractal geometry to the design of error correction codes, specifically addressing the challenges posed by high-dimensional data propagation through complex, non-linear systems. We propose a novel code utilizing self-similarity within a fractal structure to enhance error detection and correction capabilities, surpassing the limitations of traditional coding methods. The core mechanism involves creating a code that dynamically adapts its structure based on the detected error patterns, offering improved resilience to noise and distortion across a broader range of frequencies and spatial scales. This research investigates the potential of fractal coding to provide a fundamentally new approach to data error correction, with a focus on robustness and adaptability to complex data environments. The paper details the design of the fractal code, its error correction mechanisms, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness in detecting and correcting errors in simulated high-dimensional data.

title: Title: Quantum-Enhanced Diffusion for Signal Processing
abstract: Quantum-enhanced diffusion, a novel approach leveraging quantum mechanics to optimize diffusion-based signal processing algorithms, presents a significant advancement in data recovery rates. This paper explores the potential of quantum tunneling to accelerate the diffusion process, ultimately enhancing the efficiency of data extraction. We detail the theoretical framework underpinning this technique, outlining the fundamental principles of quantum tunneling and their application to signal processing. We present a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's design, demonstrating its potential advantages over traditional diffusion methods. This work establishes a strong foundation for future research and development in this field, potentially revolutionizing data recovery techniques.

title: Quantum-Inspired Optimization of Large-Scale Distributed Systems
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum-inspired optimization techniques to the complex problem of routing and scheduling tasks within large-scale distributed systems. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with the inherent challenges of distributed environments, including high dimensionality, non-linearity, and dynamic changes. We propose a novel framework that borrows concepts from quantum mechanics – specifically superposition and interference – to enhance decision-making processes. The core idea involves representing task assignments as quantum states and utilizing interference patterns to identify optimal scheduling configurations. Mathematical formulations and algorithmic approaches are presented, demonstrating the potential of this approach to minimize communication latency, reduce resource contention, and ultimately improve the overall performance of distributed systems. The methodology offers a fundamentally different perspective, moving beyond purely classical optimization paradigms and offering a potentially transformative solution for optimizing complex distributed systems.

title: A Programming Language Based on Biological Neural Networks
abstract: This paper introduces a novel programming language, tentatively named "Synapse," designed to leverage the principles and structure of biological neural networks for software development. Synapse aims to provide a more intuitive and potentially more efficient programming paradigm by directly mapping program logic onto neural network connections and activation patterns. The core mechanism involves creating a computational model inspired by the biological brain, allowing for inherent parallelism and adaptive learning capabilities. This approach represents a departure from traditional, sequential programming models and explores a fundamentally new way to conceive and execute software. The paper details the key features and design considerations of Synapse, focusing on the mapping between code and neural network structures, and highlights the potential benefits of this bio-inspired programming approach.

The paper details the key features and design considerations of Synapse, focusing on the mapping between code and neural network structures, and highlights the potential benefits of this bio-inspired programming approach.

title: Bio-Inspired Chaotic Computation: A Novel Approach to Parallel Processing and Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel computational paradigm based on bio-inspired chaotic systems, specifically designed to address the challenges of parallel processing and optimization. The core idea is to mimic the chaotic behavior observed in biological neural networks, leveraging the inherent sensitivity to initial conditions characteristic of chaotic systems. This approach offers a fundamentally different strategy compared to conventional computing architectures, providing a potentially more efficient and robust method for complex problem-solving. The proposed model utilizes self-organizing maps (SOMs) in conjunction with nonlinear dynamical equations to generate chaotic dynamics, facilitating parallel search and optimization. We demonstrate the feasibility of this approach and highlight its potential advantages through a theoretical framework. The key contributions of this work lie in the integration of biological inspiration with chaotic dynamics to achieve efficient parallel computation.

title: Title: Quantum Simulation of Biological Metabolic Pathways via Adaptive Quantum States
abstract: Quantum simulation offers a revolutionary approach to modeling complex biological systems, particularly metabolic pathways, which currently demand immense computational resources. This paper explores the application of quantum computing to simulate these pathways, focusing on the development of a novel method for dynamically adapting quantum states to mimic the intricate changes inherent within metabolic processes. We propose a quantum circuit design that mimics the key steps of a metabolic pathway, leveraging adaptive quantum states to represent and evolve the energy levels, thereby providing a pathway to significantly enhance the fidelity and accuracy of simulations. The core claim is that this method will enable a more thorough investigation of metabolic dynamics, offering unprecedented insights into biological function and potential therapeutic targets.

title: Non-Euclidean Geometry of Quantum State Transfer Models
abstract: Non-Euclidean Geometry presents a novel approach to quantum state transfer modeling, offering a framework for analyzing the evolution of quantum states through complex geometric transformations. This paper proposes a dynamic model leveraging non-Euclidean geometry to capture the intricate interplay of quantum entanglement and spatial distribution, leading to a new quantum state transfer algorithm. The core mechanism focuses on mapping initial quantum states to non-Euclidean spaces, enabling the exploration of novel quantum pathways and efficient state transitions. We investigate the implications of this approach through a series of simulations and preliminary results demonstrating the potential for enhanced state fidelity and adaptability compared to traditional approaches. This work offers a promising avenue for advancing our understanding of quantum phenomena and developing robust quantum control techniques.

title: Verdict On AGI: A Critical Audit of OpenAI's Claim to Have Achieved Artificial General Intelligence
abstract: Verdict on AGI is a 47-page critical audit of OpenAI's claim — anchored in the August 2026 TIME interview with Sam Altman and the September 3, 2026 release of GPT-6 Astra — that the company has achieved or is about to achieve Artificial General Intelligence. The paper applies a strict four-tier verdict scale (HONORED / PARTIALLY HONORED / EXPOSED AS MARKETING / INVALID) to eight major OpenAI AGI-anchored claims from 2018 through September 2026, using Definition D (flexible, sample-efficient generalization to genuinely novel environments) as the primary bar. The central finding: across all eight claims, zero meet the strict bar, two are partially honored, five are exposed as marketing, and one is invalid; Astra is not an exception but the eighth instance of a recurring pattern with five structural defects — no operational definition, selected benchmarks, closed-door demos, executive estimates without methodology, and internal designations coinciding with commercial pressure. The strongest evidence-anchored AGI claim is not OpenAI's — it is Anthropic's, which as of September 5, 2026 holds the #1 spot on BenchAlign (Claude Fable 5.1) and leads SWE-bench Verified through Claude Opus 4.7 (87.6%), backed by the only public binding safety commitment (the Responsible Scaling Policy with ASL-3 deployment-pause clause) and the September 1, 2026 Enterprise Frontier Safeguards. The paper's secondary contribution is a current-as-of-September-5-2026 model lineup covering OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra and GPT-5.6 Sol, Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.1 and Opus 5, Google DeepMind's Gemini 3.8 Flash, xAI's Grok 4.6, Meta's Muse Spark 1.3, DeepSeek's V4-Pro 0813, Alibaba's Qwen3.8-Max, and Mistral's Medium 3.5. The pattern itself is the finding: when the most consequential capability claim in 21st-century technology is examined against its own published evidence, AGI is what OpenAI says it is, and what OpenAI says it is keeps moving.

title: ISOM: Isometric State Operator Manifold
abstract: ISOM: Isometric State Operator Manifold (ISOM-R2 Multi-Million-Token Architecture) ISOM (Isometric State Operator Manifold) introduces the ISOM-R2 bounded-memory execution architecture designed to eliminate the linear Key-Value cache memory wall and quadratic prefill bottleneck of standard Transformer models across multi-million-token contexts. In conventional Transformer architectures, storing a 2.15M to 2.77M token Key-Value cache requires between 57.3 GiB and 137.3 GiB of GPU VRAM for the KV cache alone. Powered by the ISOM-R2 engine, the four models in the Ael Model Family stream and synthesize across 2,147,447 to 2,774,027 continuous real tokens on a single NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB GPU in 7.42 to 13.94 seconds while strictly bounding the active GPU attention window to 2,112 tokens (+0.01 GB to +0.09 GB streaming KV overhead). 1. Core Mathematical & Systems Formulation (ISOM-R2) Hierarchical Paged Virtual SVD Cache (ISOMR2VirtualSVDCache): Incoming token streams of length N > 2 × 106 are partitioned into 2,048-token pages. Evicted pages are projected into compact low-rank spectral bases, while the active GPU KV cache holds strictly L_active = 64 + 2048 = 2112 tokens (64 attention sinks + 2,048 active sliding window). Lie-Manifold Orthogonal Transport on SO(d) & O(1) Algebraic Rollback: Recurrent state transitions evolve on the Special Orthogonal Lie group via skew-symmetric generators A_t = -A_t^T in so(d) using the closed-form Cayley transform: U_t = (I - 0.5 * A_t)^(-1) (I + 0.5 * A_t) in SO(d) Because U_t is strictly orthogonal (||U_t^T U_t - I||_F <= 4.47e-05), multi-step reasoning trajectories preserve exact state norm and admit closed-form O(1) multi-hop state inversion: h_0 = U_hop^T (h_K - Delta_H) Entity-Balanced Multi-Hop Lexical + Spectral Retrieval (ISOMR2Engine): Each 2,048-token page is indexed with structural class/function definition signatures and per-entity inverse-document-frequency (IDF) weights, enabling 100% multi-hop page recall across inter-module gaps exceeding 1.39 million tokens with zero distractor pages. 2. Audited Multi-Million-Token Benchmarks (Ael Model Family on NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB) All four models in the Ael Model Family are evaluated on unpadded, real-world open-source repositories (huggingface/transformers, sympy/sympy, and django/django). Interactive telemetry and verbatim execution logs are available at the official benchmark space: https://huggingface.co/spaces/Prannesshkva/ISOM-Benchmark.
